cases.sentence: Но он не успел еще сообразить того, что полковник был убит, что кричавший «братцы!» был пленный, что в глазах его был заколот штыком в спину ___.
cases.explain: «другой солдат» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: But he had not time to realize that the colonel had been killed, that the soldier shouting “Brothers!” was a prisoner, and that another man had been bayoneted in the back before his eyes, for hardly had he run into the redoubt before a thin, sallow-faced, perspiring man in a blue uniform rushed on him sword in hand, shouting something. Instinctively guarding against the shock—for they had been running together at full speed before they saw one another—Pierre put out his hands and seized the man (a French officer) by the shoulder with one hand and by the throat with the other. The officer, dropping his sword, seized Pierre by his collar.

cases.sentence: Едва он вбежал в окоп, как худощавый, желтый, с ___ человек в синем мундире, со шпагой в руке, набежал на него, крича что-то.
cases.explain: «потным лицом» — after the preposition «с», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.

cases.sentence: Пьер, инстинктивно обороняясь от толчка, так как они не видав разбежались друг против друга, выставил руки и схватил этого человека (это был ___) одною рукой за плечо, другою за горло.
cases.explain: «французский офицер» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.

cases.sentence: Но очевидно французский офицер более склонялся к мысли, что в плен взят он, потому что ___ Пьера, движимая невольным страхом, всё крепче и крепче сжимала его горло.
cases.explain: «сильная рука» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: For some seconds they gazed with frightened eyes at one another’s unfamiliar faces and both were perplexed at what they had done and what they were to do next. “Am I taken prisoner or have I taken him prisoner?” each was thinking. But the French officer was evidently more inclined to think he had been taken prisoner because Pierre’s strong hand, impelled by instinctive fear, squeezed his throat ever tighter and tighter. The Frenchman was about to say something, when just above their heads, terrible and low, a cannon ball whistled, and it seemed to Pierre that the French officer’s head had been torn off, so swiftly had he ducked it.

cases.sentence: Француз что-то хотел сказать, как вдруг над самою головой их низко и страшно просвистело ядро, и Пьеру показалось, что голова ___ оторвана: так быстро он согнул ее.
cases.explain: «французского офицера» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.

cases.sentence: Но не успел он сойти вниз, как навстречу ему показались плотные толпы бегущих ___, которые, падая, спотыкаясь и крича, весело и бурно бежали на батарею.
cases.explain: «русских солдат» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: (This was the attack for which Ermólov claimed the credit, declaring that only his courage and good luck made such a feat possible: it was the attack in which he was said to have thrown some St. George’s Crosses he had in his pocket into the battery for the first soldiers to take who got there.)

cases.sentence: С батареи свезли пленных, в том числе раненого ___, которого окружили офицеры.
cases.explain: «французского генерала» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: The prisoners were brought down from the battery and among them was a wounded French general, whom the officers surrounded. Crowds of wounded—some known to Pierre and some unknown—Russians and French, with faces distorted by suffering, walked, crawled, and were carried on stretchers from the battery. Pierre again went up onto the knoll where he had spent over an hour, and of that family circle which had received him as a member he did not find a single one. There were many dead whom he did not know, but some he recognized. The young officer still sat in the same way, bent double, in a pool of blood at the edge of the earth wall. The red-faced man was still twitching, but they did not carry him away.
